## The well-balanced face positivity fallback {#sec-ch08-wbface}

<!-- PROVENANCE
pin: snapy@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0 (chengcli/snapy)
sources: OUTLINE.md 8.9
status: draft
-->

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- In the well-balanced $x_1$ path the face state is a reference plus a perturbation, and the sum can go negative.
- Switch: active with the well-balanced reference; the ordinary face floors are switched off there.
- A non-positive face pressure falls back to the reference pressure.
- A non-positive face density falls back to the *adjacent cell's* density, not to the reference.
- At rest the perturbation vanishes, so the fallback never fires and well-balancing is preserved.
:::

The well-balanced path reconstructs a perturbation about a hydrostatic reference and adds the reference
back at the face. Near the top of a column the reference is tiny and a nonlinear overshoot in the
perturbation can take the sum below zero. This fallback catches that, and the choice of what to fall
back to is the interesting part.

### Derivation

The pressure case is the simple one: a face pressure that comes out non-positive is replaced by the
reference pressure at that face, at `psf_lo` ([`hydro_forward.cpp:357-360`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L357-L360)). The reference is positive by
construction, and at rest the perturbation is zero, so the condition is never met and the well-balanced
property survives untouched.

The density case is where a reasonable-looking choice is wrong, and the code comment at
`dsf` ([`hydro_forward.cpp:362-367`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L362-L367)) records why from experience rather than from theory. Falling
back to the reference density fails when the reference overestimates the density aloft: a
bottom-anchored isentrope did so by orders of magnitude, and every floor event at a reflecting top wall
then became a large spurious wall impedance. The fallback is therefore the adjacent cell's density,
which is a real local value rather than an extrapolated reference.

A second detail in the same block is a latent-bug note worth carrying into the report. The shift along
$x_1$ uses edge replication rather than a circular roll, and the comment at
`density` ([`hydro_forward.cpp:368-373`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L368-L373)) says plainly that the circular word is not consumed today, but
would become live the moment a caller changed the face range. That is a hazard recorded in the code and
not a current defect.

### Numerical method

The block is `copy_` ([`hydro_forward.cpp:350-372`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L350-L372)). The reconstruction that feeds it is called with
floors switched off at `wtmp` ([`hydro_forward.cpp:346-348`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L346-L348)), precisely because the ordinary
reconstruction floors would clamp a legitimate negative perturbation; this fallback replaces them for
this path.

### Tests

No test isolates the fallback. Its no-op-at-rest property is covered indirectly by the well-balanced
tests of @sec-ch05, which would fail if it fired on a resting column.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- The density fallback substitutes a neighbouring cell's density into a face state. That is a local
  value, but it is not the reconstruction's answer, and nothing measures the error it introduces when
  it fires.
:::

1. **Hypothesis, from a run not reproduced here.** That the reference-density fallback caused a large
   spurious wall impedance is recorded in the code comment from a bottom-anchored isentrope case. This
   chapter cites that reasoning; it does not reproduce the run.
2. **A latent hazard.** The edge-replication note describes a wraparound that is unreachable with
   today's face range. It is recorded because the range is the only thing keeping it unreachable.
